concepts.name: 织梦蛾
concepts.title: E  SOMNUS LOOM
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Premium original retro-futurist mechanical desktop sculpture concept sheet for MagicDesk. Cream glazed porcelain, polished nickel and dark brushed steel, tiny oxide-red hardware, precision pivots, restrained amber/red light, excellent industrial detailing, clean materials without heavy grime. Grounded believable connected mechanical assemblies with visible axles. A single shared low circular HELIOS pedestal in every view: stepped dark metal rim, ivory curved front control fascia, seven round tactile buttons with the red X always at far right, circular top mounting socket; same diameter and height. Pedestal design must remain extremely close to the supplied reference. No levitating base, no game controller, no screen or UI overlay, no left/right selection arrows, no blue-purple neon, no magic runes. Neutral charcoal studio background and realistic studio render lighting. This is a visual design proposal, not a finished model. Wide 3:2 detailed board: large hero view occupying left 60%, top-right action view, bottom-right coherent exploded assembly view. Same object and same pedestal across views, full object visible without clipping. Small elegant cream condensed headings. Text only the exact title and 'REST', 'ACTIVE', 'ASSEMBLY'.
Reference image is ONLY the design anchor for the fixed pedestal and material family. Replace the entire egg above the pedestal with an original anchored mechanical moth-shaped optical weaving instrument, SOMNUS LOOM. Long slender ivory thorax attached to a short pedestal mast, two delicate bifurcated chrome antennae, four broad articulated wings (two upper, two lower) made of layered ceramic fan-blades over intricate nickel ribs. Wings have oval cutouts and micro hinge rods, no soft fur, no realistic insect organs. REST: wings fold upright close to body like a narrow ceremonial mantle, asymmetric head tilt. ACTIVE: four wings open into a wide elegant moth silhouette, inner spools physically pull a few taut glowing amber filaments between wing ribs forming a fine geometric woven veil; transparent negative spaces remain, not a particle cloud. Wing span at full deployment is about 1.8 times pedestal diameter. ASSEMBLY: the same four wing units separate slightly along hinge axes, blades and spools shown as logical modules still aligned with the mast, base remains assembled. Signature is living wing choreography and light-thread weaving, NOT a glowing spherical core. The object stays mounted; no flight, propellers, drones, weapons, or cockpit. Exact title 'E  SOMNUS LOOM'.

Reference image is ONLY the fixed pedestal and material family; replace the egg above it completely. Create LAGRANGE BALANCE, an uncanny kinetic gravity instrument with a strongly asymmetrical open silhouette. A single sweeping ivory C-shaped structural arm rises from the rear-left mounting socket, opening toward the right. A fine chrome double-parallelogram linkage spans the opening and carries two visibly different counterweights: one polished nickel teardrop and one ivory faceted rectangular prism, both physically linked to independent gimbals and slender rods. Small red analog inclinometer mounted on the C-arm. No central orb, no egg, no flower. REST: both weights hang downward, linkage folded within the C. ACTIVE: linkage unfolds into a dramatic impossible-looking sideways balance; one weight climbs up, the other projects horizontally, both attached and counterpoised, a hair-thin amber vertical reference beam through the empty center shows the deflection; beautiful open negative space. ASSEMBLY: C-arm splits into three ceramic-faced segments exposing continuous chrome spine; linkage modules and two counterweights align with their pins for reassembly. Pedestal does not change. A futuristic laboratory heirloom, not an ordinary scale with two bowls. Exact title 'F  LAGRANGE BALANCE'.

Reference image is ONLY the fixed pedestal and material family; completely replace the egg above it. Invent TEMPEST ORGAN, a miniature machine that composes contained thunderstorms. Upper sculpture is an asymmetric ascending array of FIVE tall vacuum resonator pipes, each a narrow smoke-clear glass tube with smooth ivory segmented ceramic collars, polished chrome end caps and curved copper induction windings. Their heights form a bold slanted skyline, not a symmetrical crown. All five are connected by a low curved nickel manifold and a folding ivory acoustic hood, visibly mounted to the shared pedestal; no piano keyboard. REST: hood folded closely behind the pipes, dim ember filaments inside each distinct tube, tiny analog pressure dials at tube feet. ACTIVE: hood divides into three linked curved baffles which open behind the tubes; small connected electrode arms pivot inward; vivid thin red-orange electrical filaments jump BETWEEN actual electrode tips and glow inside the glass in sequential rhythm, controlled beautiful confined energy. A single delicate steam release at the manifold, no smoky cloud hiding mechanisms. ASSEMBLY: all five complete tube cartridges lift vertically off corresponding sockets, three baffles open from hinges, manifold stays anchored, retain exactly five tubes and coherent positions. More retro scientific musical instrument than weapon, no floating orb, no organ pipes covering the pedestal buttons. Exact title 'H  TEMPEST ORGAN'.

control_panel_revisions.E: Replace ONLY the front control fascia in ALL THREE views with a moth-weaving instrument panel: three distinct central controls consisting of a pair of slender ivory wing-shaped rocker paddles, a small dark knurled tension wheel with a red index mark, and a short horizontal nickel shuttle slider. These are real raised 3D controls mounted in the ivory fascia, not printed icons. Keep one small power stud at the left and a separate red X exit control at the far right. Remove the repeated row of seven identical round HELIOS buttons. Preserve the exact upper moth, four wings, spools, posture, background, labels, panel layout, base body's silhouette and size. Preserve Atomic Heart inspired retro-future Soviet laboratory biotechnical language: smooth milk-white porcelain, bright nickel, red enamel accents, physical mechanisms; no neon dashboard.
control_panel_revisions.F: Replace ONLY the front control fascia in ALL THREE views with a gravity calibration panel: a short nickel brake lever in a curved travel slot, a large ridged ivory balance wheel with fine red calibration ticks, and one square ceramic pulse key; a small recessed analog deflection gauge between them is an indicator, not a screen. Keep a discreet power stud at far left and separate red X exit control at far right. The controls must have different actual 3D geometries; remove the seven identical round buttons. Preserve all upper C-shaped structures, articulated rods and counterweights, composition and existing labels exactly. Same base outer shell and size. Atomic Heart-inspired milk-white porcelain, nickel skeleton and Soviet retrofuture experimental laboratory character; no fantasy motifs.
control_panel_revisions.G: Replace ONLY the front control fascia in ALL THREE views with a dimensional folio control cassette: three slim ivory page-shaped rocker tabs at slightly staggered heights, one toothed nickel page-index thumbwheel, and a little red archive-seal toggle under a metal guard. Keep discreet power stud at far left and separate red X exit control at far right. Give these actual distinct 3D shapes; remove the repeated seven circular HELIOS buttons. Preserve the book, spine, exact page mechanisms, golden optical threads, composition and labels. Keep the same circular base body dimensions. Strong Atomic Heart-inspired retrofuturistic industrial biotechnology design using glossy milk-white porcelain, nickel and red enamel; avoid generic HUD panels.
